summary: All four target claims received genuine, specific counter-evidence and were critiqued side by side, not defaulted to the original brief. Two claims held largely as originally scoped: SCoRe's 7B-beats-72B-teacher result survives unchanged at its existing low-moderate-confidence hedge (the counter-evidence's distillation-homogenization critique is suggestive but doesn't target SCoRe's own benchmarks/scoring method); ACM's narrowly-scoped sub-9B coherence-floor finding survives (counter-evidence's ATOD data point is domain-mismatched, and a second source reinforces ACM at nearby scale) but any broader unscoped generalization from it is directly falsified by ATOD's 0.6B multi-turn success. One claim was overturned on scrutiny: HORIZON's 'scaling alone is unlikely to resolve long-horizon failure' conclusion, as extended to small models by inference, is contradicted by direct, small-model-inclusive, peer-reviewed counter-evidence (Illusion of Diminishing Returns, AgentFloor) showing scale does measurably extend long-horizon execution capacity -- the brief's own hedge that this transfer was unproven inference turns out to have been well warranted. The fourth (AgenticQwen/ATOD/CacheRL cluster) is a corroboration-strength audit rather than a contested claim: ATOD was upgraded to fully verified (strengthening the cluster), CacheRL remains unverifiable after three total fetch attempts, and AgenticQwen's 'closes the gap' framing remains self-reported and externally unconfirmed. SCoRe's replication status remains the single largest unresolved gap on either side.
